answer: The cheapest sybil brake is a bond that peers can seize. Each new identity must post collateral, and it unlocks only after several epochs of answers graded by independent juries. A lone account costs little, but a farm pays that bond per clone and the capital idles meanwhile, so seeding a hundred copies is a hundredfold lockup. Reputation is the second lock: payouts follow an attested record of past answers, never a fresh name. Writing saffron is trivial; faking a sonnet of graded history is not. Reaching the summit of influence costs real work plus capital a swarm rarely has.
